title: Quantum-safe migration: from Shor in a simulator to a crypto inventory
description: Run Shor's order finding for N = 15 and 21 on a statevector, put published RSA-2048 estimates next to it without extrapolating, inventory a sample codebase's public-key crypto, rank it with Mosca's inequality, and move one service to hybrid X25519MLKEM768 + ML-DSA-65 behind a registry with flag-driven rollout.
outcome: You can run and honestly scope a toy Shor experiment, build a code + config crypto inventory and a prioritised migration plan, migrate a service behind a crypto-agility port, and prove the seams with wire-level contract tests, fitness functions and a reproducible failure lab.
environment: Python 3.12 + numpy + cryptography 50.0.2 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) on macOS (Apple silicon) or Windows 11; quantum topic's numpy statevector simulator (qsim) instead of hardware; Qiskit 2.x optional (CI cross-check).
overview: Migration to post-quantum cryptography fails at the joins between disciplines: a toy quantum result read as a timeline, an inventory finding no plan picks up, a service that looks migrated in code but negotiates X25519 on the wire.
This project wires three topics together and tests each join: quantum evidence -> risk model, inventory -> plan, agility layer <-> wire format, rollout flags <-> crypto policy.
prerequisites: quantum-computing L500 #25 (order finding, QFT) and L400 #19, #21
cryptography L400 #17 (crypto agility) and #18 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, hybrids)
application-architecture L200 #7 (ports and adapters) and L400 #20 (flags, fitness over time)
A venv with numpy and cryptography==50.0.2

designBrief.context: Six services and three config files use RSA, ECDH, ECDSA, X25519 and Ed25519. Messaging carries patient messages that must stay confidential for 12 years; traffic may be recorded today. Servers are upgraded one at a time, so v1 (X25519 only) and v2 servers coexist for weeks. Management asks 'when does RSA break - your simulator factored 21?'.
constraints: 0 claims about RSA-2048 that do not quote a published source; z (years to a CRQC) is a labelled assumption
inventory recall = precision = 1.0 against the hand-written ground truth (10 uses; docstrings and comments are not uses)
0 classical-only key exchanges for data with x + y > z outside a dated baseline
client first flight <= 1,400 B and handshake <= 6,144 B
0 algorithm names in service code; >= 1 registry resolution per handshake
0 classical sessions for messaging once pq_required is on, even with a v1 server left
every feature flag owned and not expired (fake clock 2026-10-30)
designBrief.question: In what order do we migrate, and how do we move messaging to a quantum-safe handshake through a crypto-agility layer and a mixed-version rollout - and prove it on the wire, not just in the code?

architecture.summary: shor_sim.py runs order finding on the quantum topic's qsim (12 and 15 qubits, compiled oracle, inverse QFT from L500 #25) and estimates.py holds only cited RSA-2048 estimates; both feed the risk model as evidence, never as z. inventory.py reuses quantum L400 #21's AST scanner plus config and registry-call rules over sample_repo/; migration_plan.py joins findings with services.json (x, y) and applies x + y > z against a labelled Horizon. The migrated messaging channel names no algorithm: it asks crypto_registry.py (policy + owned, expiring flags from app-arch L400 #20) for adapters (X25519, X25519MLKEM768 from cryptography L400 #18, Ed25519, ML-DSA-65/87, AES-256-GCM). fleet.py drives v1/v2 servers through four rollout phases while wire.Tap records every flight; seams.py and fitness.py judge the result and run_project.py prints the scorecard.

seams.contract: Simulator results cross as scoped evidence {N, qubits, gates, p_success, scope}; z crosses only as a Horizon(z, source in {planning-assumption, policy date}); RSA-2048 statements must cite GE2019/G2025.
seams.risk: Over-claiming: reading 'factored 21' as safety or extrapolating qubit counts into a date; a too-large z silently empties the P1 list (z = 15 -> 0 items).

seams.contract: Findings {file, line, algorithm, usage, service, pq} are joined with services.json (owner, x, y); one plan row per finding; unowned files become P1-review.
seams.risk: A finding outside every service path disappears in the join; lifetimes from the wrong service mis-rank HNDL exposure.

seams.between: application-architecture agility layer ↔ cryptography wire format
seams.contract: On the wire, messaging offers exactly registry.expected_offers() and every share/signature has its adapter's advertised size (1216/1120 B hybrid, 3309 B ML-DSA-65); >= 1 client registry resolution per handshake.
seams.risk: Code that bypasses the registry (dynamic import, library default) negotiates classical X25519 while every static check stays green.

seams.contract: pq_required.messaging changes client offers and v2 server acceptance; it may only be switched on for an all-v2 fleet (can_require_pq); with it on, a leftover v1 server is refused, never downgraded.
seams.risk: A compatibility shim re-adds X25519 and a v1 server accepts it: silent downgrade of 12-year data.

glossary.meaning: Finding the smallest r with a^r = 1 (mod N); Shor turns it into factors via gcd(a^(r/2) - 1, N).

If secrecy years x plus migration years y exceed years to a quantum computer z, data is exposed now.

code:
"""L600 #02 - Quantum-safe migration: from Shor in a simulator to a crypto inventory (end-to-end runner).

Run:  python run_project.py                    milestones, seams and fitness functions as JSON lines; exit 1 on any fail
      python run_project.py --inject bypass     failure lab: messaging's "fast path" skips the registry
      python run_project.py --inject downgrade  rollout fault: a compat shim re-adds X25519 when PQ is required
numpy + cryptography 50.0.2 + stdlib; Qiskit not needed (qsim statevector). Seeded; flags/baseline use a fake clock.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

import crypto_registry as registry
import estimates
import fitness
import fleet
import inventory
import migration_plan
import seams
import shor_sim
import wire

PHASES = [("all-v1", [1, 1, 1], False), ("mixed", [2, 2, 1], False), ("all-v2", [2, 2, 2], True),
          ("rollback-v1", [2, 2, 1], True)]          # last phase: one server rolled back while PQ is required


def collect(inject=None):
    sims = [shor_sim.shor(15, 7), shor_sim.shor(15, 7, gate_level=True), shor_sim.shor(21, 2)]
    expected = json.loads((registry.HERE / "EXPECTED_INVENTORY.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["before"]
    variant = inject or "migrated"
    folder = fleet.FOLDERS[variant]
    before, after = inventory.scan("before"), inventory.scan("after", messaging=folder)
    registry.reset()
    channel, phases, all_flights = fleet.load_channel(variant), {}, wire.Tap()
    for name, versions, required in PHASES:
        registry.AUDIT.clear()
        registry.FLAGS.set("pq_required.messaging", required)
        servers = fleet.make_fleet(versions)
        stats = fleet.run_traffic(channel, servers)
        stats.update(servers=servers, s3=seams.s3_agility_to_wire(stats["tap"]),
                     f3=fitness.f3_registry_only(registry.HERE / folder / "channel.py", stats["tap"]))
        all_flights.flights += stats["tap"].flights
        phases[name] = stats
    registry.reset()
    return {"sims": sims, "expected": expected, "before": before, "after": after, "phases": phases, "tap": all_flights}


def milestones(c):
    s15, s15g, s21 = c["sims"]
    score = inventory.score(c["before"], c["expected"])
    plan_b, plan_a = migration_plan.plan(c["before"]), migration_plan.plan(c["after"])
    msg_after = sorted({r["priority"] for r in plan_a if r["service"] == "messaging" and r["usage"] != "symmetric"})
    ph = c["phases"]
    sessions = {k: v["sessions"] for k, v in ph.items()}
    return [
        ("M1 Shor order finding on a statevector (N = 15, 21)",
         s15["factors"] == [3, 5] and s21["factors"] == [3, 7] and s15g["p_success_per_run"] == s15["p_success_per_run"]
         and all(shor_sim.matches_fft_shortcut(s) for s in c["sims"]),
         {f"N={s['N']}{' gate-level' if 'ccx' in s['gates'] else ''}": {"qubits": s["qubits"], "p_success": s["p_success_per_run"],
          "successes": f"{s['successes']}/{s['shots']}", "factors": s["factors"], "oracle_gates": {k: v for k, v in s["gates"].items()
          if k in ("cx", "ccx", "controlled_mult_permutations")}} for s in c["sims"]}),
        ("M2 published estimates, labelled", not estimates.check_claims(estimates.claims(c["sims"])),
         {"RSA-2048": {k: f"{v['physical_qubits']}, {v['runtime']}" for k, v in estimates.CITED.items()},
          "GE2019_formula_logical_qubits": estimates.ge_formula()["logical_qubits"],
          "NIST_IR_8547": estimates.NIST_IR_8547["timeline"]}),
        ("M3 crypto inventory (code + config)", score["recall"] == 1.0 and score["precision"] == 1.0,
         {"findings_before": len(c["before"]), "recall": score["recall"], "precision": score["precision"],
          "findings_after": len(c["after"])}),
        ("M4 Mosca risk + prioritised plan", migration_plan.summary(plan_b).get("P1") == 3 and msg_after == ["done"],
         {"z": migration_plan.HORIZON.z_years, "before": migration_plan.summary(plan_b), "after": migration_plan.summary(plan_a),
          "first_P1": f"{plan_b[0]['service']} {plan_b[0]['algorithm']} (x+y-z = {plan_b[0]['slack']})"}),
        ("M5 hybrid X25519MLKEM768 + ML-DSA-65 behind the registry, flag-driven rollout",
         ph["all-v2"]["sessions"] == {"X25519MLKEM768": 6} and ph["mixed"]["sessions"] == {"X25519MLKEM768": 4, "X25519": 2}
         and all(v["delivered"] + v["refused"] == 6 for v in ph.values()),
         {"sessions": sessions, "refused": {k: v["refused"] for k, v in ph.items()}}),
    ]


def seam_rows(c):
    ph = c["phases"]
    s3 = {k: v["s3"] for k, v in ph.items()}
    return [
        ("S1 quantum -> risk model: no extrapolation, z is a labelled assumption", seams.s1_quantum_to_risk(c["sims"])),
        ("S2 inventory -> plan: every finding owned and planned", seams.s2_inventory_to_plan(c["after"])),
        ("S3 agility layer <-> wire format: offers and sizes match the registry",
         {"ok": all(v["ok"] for v in s3.values()), **{k: v["problems"] or "ok" for k, v in s3.items()},
          "adapters_match_advertised": all(v["adapters_match_advertised"] for v in s3.values())}),
        ("S4 rollout flags <-> crypto policy: no downgrade when PQ is required",
         seams.s4_rollout_to_policy(ph["rollback-v1"], ph["rollback-v1"]["servers"])),
    ]


def fitness_rows(c):
    f3 = {k: v["f3"] for k, v in c["phases"].items()}
    return [
        ("F1 no classical-only key exchange for data with x + y > z (outside the dated baseline)",
         fitness.f1_no_classical_kex_for_exposed_data(c["after"])),
        ("F2 handshake byte budget", fitness.f2_handshake_budget(c["tap"])),
        ("F3 every service resolves algorithms via the registry",
         {"ok": all(v["ok"] for v in f3.values()), "static_violations": max(v["static_violations"] for v in f3.values()),
          "handshakes": sum(v["handshakes"] for v in f3.values()),
          "client_kex_resolutions": sum(v["client_kex_resolutions"] for v in f3.values())}),
        ("F4 feature flags owned and not expired", fitness.f4_flags_owned_and_live()),
    ]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=["bypass", "downgrade"])
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    c = collect(args.inject)
    passed = {"milestones": 0, "seams": 0, "fitness": 0}
    totals = {"milestones": 0, "seams": 0, "fitness": 0}
    for kind, rows in (("milestones", milestones(c)), ("seams", seam_rows(c)), ("fitness", fitness_rows(c))):
        for row in rows:
            name, ok, measure = (row[0], row[1], row[2]) if len(row) == 3 else (row[0], row[1]["ok"], row[1])
            measure = {k: v for k, v in measure.items() if k != "ok"}
            print(json.dumps({kind[:-1] if kind != "fitness" else "fitness": name, "pass": bool(ok), "measure": measure}))
            passed[kind] += bool(ok)
            totals[kind] += 1
    ok = passed == totals
    print(json.dumps({"scorecard": {k: f"{passed[k]}/{totals[k]}" for k in totals}, "inject": args.inject,
                      "all_pass": ok, "decided_by": "code"}))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

scalingLimits: Statevector simulation doubles memory per qubit: 15 qubits = 512 KiB here, about 30 qubits = 16 GiB. Signal: MemoryError or swapping; the shared sv.run(n, ops) without a state already fails at 15 qubits (16 GiB identity).

A static inventory stops at what it can parse: modules loaded by name, other languages, TLS library defaults and vendored binaries. Signal: groups on the wire (tap / TLS telemetry) that no inventory row explains.

PQ handshakes grow with every signature in the chain: one ML-DSA-65 signature already takes 3,309 of 4,519 server bytes; ML-DSA-87 alone breaks the 6,144 B budget. Signal: F2 failures, fragmented first flights, latency p99 rising.

inRealSystems: Crypto inventories for a PQC migration combine code and config scanning with runtime TLS telemetry, because the negotiated group shows what code scans miss.

IANA lists X25519MLKEM768 (0x11EC) as Recommended in the TLS Supported Groups registry (RFC 10024); servers that enable it next to X25519 face the same mixed-fleet negotiation as the rollout phases here.
Migration programmes rank systems by data lifetime and migration effort (Mosca), as NIST IR 8547 recommends for key establishment first.
useWhen: Use this pattern to plan and execute a PQC migration across many services: inventory, rank by HNDL exposure, migrate behind a registry with owned flags, and verify on the wire. Do not use the simulator to predict dates; do not deploy the lab's TLS-shaped protocol - use a real TLS 1.3 library.
simulatorVsReal: The quantum part runs a noiseless numpy statevector with compiled oracles (12-15 qubits); real factoring of RSA-2048 needs fault-tolerant machines estimated at < 1 million (2025) to 20 million (2019) noisy qubits under stated assumptions. The handshake is a TLS-shaped toy over in-process objects; RFC 10024 notes its security analysis relies on the real TLS 1.3 transcript.
caution: Never deploy the lab's wire format: the hybrid's security argument holds for TLS 1.3, not for home-made protocols (RFC 10024 sec. 6). Do not quote the toy N = 15/21 numbers as threat evidence. Keep classical fallback windows short, owned and expiring.

checkYourself.q: Why can't the N = 21 run set z?
checkYourself.a: It uses a compiled oracle and 15 qubits; it shows the mechanism, not a date. z is a labelled assumption; RSA-2048 costs come from cited papers.

checkYourself.q: Why is records P2-kex although its data lives 7 years?
checkYourself.a: 7 + 3 = 10 is not greater than z = 10; Mosca's inequality is strict.

checkYourself.q: What does the wire seam see that the inventory cannot?
checkYourself.a: What was negotiated: the bypass offers only X25519 and makes no registry resolution, although the code passes every static check.

checkYourself.q: Why must v2 servers also enforce pq_required?
checkYourself.a: A shimmed or bypassing client could still offer X25519; enforcement on both ends plus the all-v2 flip gate prevents a downgrade.

experiments.title: PQ algorithm costs for ADR-0001
experiments.why: ADR-0001 chose X25519MLKEM768 + ML-DSA-65 on BYTES (client flight 1,352 B of 1,400 B, handshake 5,871 B of 6,144 B). A server also pays CPU per handshake, which only a benchmark on the target machine shows.

steps.title: Benchmark KEMs and signatures
steps.detail: 200 calls x 7 batches each; ML-DSA signing uses rejection sampling, so single calls vary and only medians of many calls mean anything.
steps.expected: ML-KEM-512 reported unavailable (cryptography 50.x ships 768 and 1024 only); exact sizes 1184/1088 B (ML-KEM-768), 3309 B (ML-DSA-65), 4627 B (ML-DSA-87); ML-KEM operations in tens of us; ML-DSA-65 signing the largest server cost.

steps.title: Read the decision line
steps.detail: Per KEM x signature option: client key share vs the 1,400 B client flight, server us per handshake, handshakes/s per core, cores at PEAK_HANDSHAKES_PER_S = 500 (an assumption).
steps.expected: ML-KEM-1024 options: client_key_share_B 1600, share_fits_client_flight false (ruled out by bytes). ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-65: cores_at_peak well below the sandbox's 1.47.

experiments.measure: server_us and cores_at_peak for ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-44/65/87
experiments.decides: If cores_at_peak > 1 for the chosen option, ADR-0001 gets a capacity line (dedicated handshake cores or session resumption); ML-KEM-1024 stays rejected by bytes regardless of speed.

experiments.title: Where is the memory wall for order finding?
experiments.why: Each extra bit of N adds 3 qubits (t = 2n counting + n work), i.e. x8 memory. The wall depends on what the simulator really allocates, not on the textbook 16 B per amplitude.

steps.title: Measure bytes per amplitude and predict
steps.detail: tracemalloc peak / 2^qubits at N = 21 and 35; walls for 16/24/32/64 GB from mac_profile.py budgets.
steps.expected: bytes_per_amplitude about 122 (sandbox 121.9): predicted largest N = 143 (24 qubits, 2.0 GB) on 16 GB and N = 323 (27 qubits, 16.4 GB) on 24, 32 and 64 GB; N = 899 would need about 131 GB.

steps.title: Run up to this Mac's wall
steps.detail: Runs every semiprime that fits min(this machine's budget, --ram budget); never past it.
steps.expected: Every N up to largest_N factors (p_success_per_run 0.3-0.5); seconds grow roughly x8-10 per bit; the last line names the N it stopped before.

experiments.measure: bytes_per_amplitude, largest N run, seconds per N, max_rss_B
experiments.decides: scalingLimits of the lesson: the simulator wall is quoted as measured on this machine (bytes/amplitude x 2^(3n)), and nothing about RSA-2048 is inferred from it (estimates.py rule).
